title: What figure comes from equal diagonals at four angles?
description: Four drawings are made with two equal diagonals of eight centimetres that cut each other in half, crossing at thirty, forty, ninety and one hundred forty degrees. The video draws each one by the method of the sixty degree case, finds its corners, and names the figure.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal diagonals that cut each other in half give a rectangle at any crossing angle, and a square when they cross at ninety degrees. Watch for students who think only the ninety degree crossing gives a rectangle.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 2)
video_script.why: The child draws four figures from equal diagonals that cut each other in half, checks that every crossing angle gives four right angles, and sees when the figure is also a square.
video_script.substitution: Draw the diagonal, mark its midpoint, draw the second diagonal at the crossing angle, join the ends, and find the corners as in the sixty degree case.
video_script.anchor: two equal diagonals AC and BD of 8 cm crossing at O, with the crossing angle marked
video_script.payoff_line: All four are rectangles, and the ninety degree one is a square

final_answer.value: all four are rectangles; the 90° one is a square
final_answer.spoken: all four are rectangles, and the ninety degree one is a square

maths_rules: AC = BD = 8 cm and O is the midpoint of both, so OA = OB = OC = OD = 4 cm
crossing 30 degrees: angle AOB = 30, base angles (180 - 30) / 2 = 75; angle AOD = 150, base angles (180 - 150) / 2 = 15; corner 75 + 15 = 90
crossing 40 degrees: base angles 70 and 20, corner 90
crossing 140 degrees: base angles (180 - 140) / 2 = 20 and 70, corner 90
crossing 90 degrees: base angles 45 and 45, corner 90
in general the corner is (90 - x/2) + x/2 = 90, so every figure is a rectangle
at 90 degrees the four triangles at O have legs 4 cm and 4 cm with a right angle between, so they match by SAS and all four sides are equal: a square
video_script.design: One idea: equal diagonals that bisect each other make a rectangle at every crossing angle. The anchor is the pair of diagonals with the crossing angle marked, redrawn for each angle.

<bookmark mark='other'/>The base angles are seventy five, and the other triangle gives fifteen.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>Each corner holds seventy five plus fifteen, and the other angles work the same way.

beats.on_screen: Answer: all four are rectangles; the 90° one is a square

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>All four are rectangles, and the ninety degree one is a square.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The crossing angle changes the shape, but never the right angles.
